name: Rockwell Automation

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Rockwell Automation logo (2019).svg; en.wikipedia marks the older logo.svg as previous logo)

description: Rockwell Automation sells the controllers, drives, motors, safety and sensing gear and the software that run factories, plus the engineering and support services to install and maintain them. Its Allen-Bradley hardware and FactoryTalk-type software are bought mostly through distributors and by plant operators and machine builders in discrete, hybrid and process industries. Most revenue is one-time hardware and project sales that follow customers' capital spending; software subscriptions and recurring support contracts are a smaller, faster-growing part (management targets double-digit annual recurring revenue growth).

businessLines.name: Intelligent Devices
businessLines.how: One-time hardware sales (drives, motion, safety, sensing, industrial components, configured-to-order products) to machine builders and plant operators, mostly through distributors; volume follows factory capital spending and inventory cycles.

businessLines.name: Software & Control
businessLines.how: Controllers, control and visualization software, digital twin and simulation software, and network and security infrastructure: a mix of one-time controller hardware, perpetual and subscription software licences, and recurring maintenance. Highest-margin segment.

businessLines.name: Lifecycle Services
businessLines.how: Digital consulting, engineered-to-order project work billed per project, plus recurring managed-support contracts (cybersecurity, remote monitoring, asset management) billed annually, and the Sensia oil-and-gas automation joint venture.

brands.name: Sensia (joint venture, consolidated)
brands.note: Oil-and-gas automation joint venture inside Lifecycle Services; $224M non-cash goodwill and intangible impairment in FY2025 ($110M after non-controlling interest and tax). Revenue not broken out in the 10-K text read.
